reviewer: /root main coordinator; bounded source-level behavior comparison; no runtime execution
title: Frozen business-day close exceptions versus live control-center delivery exceptions
scope: Targeted semantic comparison of CloseBusinessDayHandler.BuildDayExceptionsAsync and ControlCenterQueryService.GetExceptionsAsync, their shared ControlCenterRules.BuildExceptions routine and the two server routes. This is not an AST clone assertion. This is a narrowly additive extension to SEM-MIRROR-011, which compared live reconciliation with frozen close-snapshot/reopen behavior; it specifically compares the delivery-warning input sets and does not repeat the revision-race or reconciliation JSON questions.
decision: SOURCE-CONFIRMED INPUT-DOMAIN DIVERGENCE: the live exception query supplies current delivery rows, so shared rules can emit delivery warnings; the frozen close snapshot omits Deliveries and therefore cannot capture those warning categories. Whether that omission is a defect depends on the intended close-snapshot contract: the code separately treats delivery warnings as live operational state and does not make these warnings close blockers. Record as a conditional documentation/contract gap, not a confirmed financial defect.

behavior.common_rule: Both paths call ControlCenterRules.BuildExceptions for the financial discrepancy/refund/expense/custody/journal categories.
behavior.live_query: ControlCenterQueryService.GetExceptionsAsync loads the selected day; current delivery entities in Ready, OutForDelivery, Failed or Returned are mapped to inputs. Rules then emit ready-unassigned, failed/returned and aged-out-for-delivery warnings; states are overlaid by deterministic exception ID.
behavior.close_snapshot: CloseBusinessDayHandler invokes blockers first, then BuildDayExceptionsAsync and serializes its result in ExceptionsJson. That method passes shifts/refunds/expenses/unsettled custody/incomplete journals but omits Deliveries. BusinessDayCloseEvaluator itself has no delivery-row warning input; it checks open shifts, unsettled custody, incomplete journal, pending electronic payment, checklist and reconciliation invariants.
behavior.time_semantics: The OutForDelivery threshold is relative to current NowUtc when not explicitly supplied. Live queries recompute current warnings; a frozen close snapshot would need a deliberate as-of time if delivery warnings are added.

cross_file_call_chain: POST /api/business-day/{id}/close -> CloseBusinessDayHandler.HandleAsync -> BusinessDayCloseEvaluator.EvaluateAsync -> BuildDayExceptionsAsync -> ControlCenterRules.BuildExceptions -> serialized BusinessDayCloseSnapshot.ExceptionsJson
GET /api/business-day/{id}/exceptions -> ControlCenterQueryService.GetExceptionsAsync -> ControlCenterRules.BuildExceptions -> current exception DTOs/status overlay
counterevidence_and_limits: The live delivery exceptions are described as current per-delivery operations; a close snapshot may intentionally retain only day-close/financial exceptions.
The close evaluator does not block on the omitted warning categories, so omission does not bypass a documented close blocker based on the inspected code.
No actual closed-day snapshot or live delivery row was read; no route or database/runtime test was run.
An OutForDelivery warning changes with time, so snapshot and live results are not necessarily expected to remain equal.
Only this identified pair and shared rules were compared; no claim of repository-wide semantic completeness.
candidate_disposition: No canonical defect finding. Track as a conditional contract/documentation question: should a frozen close snapshot include contemporaneous delivery operational warnings, or is ExceptionsJson intentionally limited to closeout/financial exceptions?
recommendation: Document the snapshot contract. If delivery warnings belong in the close record, create a shared, explicit input builder/policy or pass a snapshot-time delivery projection (including NowUtc captured by the close command) and avoid replaying live time-dependent status as if historical. If snapshots are intentionally financial/closeout-only, name or document that scope clearly and keep live exception query current. Avoid consolidating the two queries without preserving their distinct time and scope semantics.
tests: Unit test BuildExceptions with each delivery state and explicit NowUtc threshold boundary.
Integration test compares live exception response and close snapshot for Ready-without-driver, Failed/Returned, and OutForDelivery just below/above 90 minutes, asserting the owner-approved scope.
Snapshot test verifies later delivery status/time changes do not mutate already serialized snapshot.
Close blocker tests confirm these operational warnings are informational unless business policy explicitly changes.
limitations: Static review only; no SQL Server or runtime tests.
Owner intent for close snapshot exception contents is not specified.

source_references.evidence: Close command runs BusinessDayCloseEvaluator, then persists BuildDayExceptionsAsync output in the frozen snapshot. BuildDayExceptionsAsync gathers financial exceptions but does not pass Deliveries to BuildExceptions.

Live day-exceptions endpoint loads current Ready/OutForDelivery/Failed/Returned delivery rows, maps them into the optional Deliveries input, calls the same rules, and overlays persisted exception status.

BuildExceptions emits warning records for Ready without driver, Failed/Returned, and OutForDelivery exceeding 90 minutes only when Deliveries input is supplied; other financial exceptions use the shared input fields.
Close POST and live exceptions GET are separately routed to the close handler and query service.
